summary: Four great coordinated projects of ʿumrān, each a field of action under the ultimate human end, not an additional canonical maqṣad.
governing_end: The Islamic account centres the human person's relation to God, not occupational prestige or aggregate productivity.
cross_cutting_principles: Maqāṣid and juristic method evaluate ends and means across every project.
Farḍ kifāya classifies specific obligations, not these four headings.
Empirical sufficiency identifies particular deficiencies, not ultimate human worth.
Technological risk, finance, formation and global interdependence cross project boundaries.
Every small programme has one primary home for navigation and may have several justified secondary links.

projects.title: Form Persons & Households
projects.short: Nurture worship, character, care and responsible family life.
projects.outcome: People and households capable of living well, caring for others and fulfilling their responsibilities.

initiatives.name: Household formation
initiatives.example: Structured family learning and intergenerational care

initiatives.name: Care and dignity
initiatives.example: Support for carers and vulnerable households

projects.method: Study lived practices, dignity, household responsibilities and continuity of care; never infer spiritual rank from employment.
projects.capacity: Mentors, caregivers, teachers, community organisers and families

projects.title: Renew Knowledge & Education
projects.short: Restore serious learning, scholarly succession and confident intellectual inquiry.
projects.outcome: Living traditions of learning: competent scholars, reliable texts, coherent teaching and mature engagement with contemporary ideas.

initiatives.name: Texts and translations
initiatives.example: Critical editions and accessible bilingual readers

initiatives.name: Integrated curricula
initiatives.example: Logic, language, jurisprudence, sciences and contemporary discourse

projects.method: Test transmission of competence and judgment, not volume of books or qualifications alone.
projects.capacity: Scholars, editors, translators, teachers, researchers and curriculum designers

projects.title: Order Just Institutions
projects.short: Renew legal discernment, trustworthy governance and accountable public life.
projects.outcome: Institutions that act justly, preserve trust, use power appropriately and support the goods they exist to provide.

initiatives.name: Living jurisprudence
initiatives.example: Research on the changing means of lawful collective provision

initiatives.name: Institutional integrity
initiatives.example: Governance, waqf, zakat and public-service standards

initiatives.name: Technology and authority
initiatives.example: Evaluation of AI, security and the delegation of judgment

projects.method: Examine law, authority, competence, consequences and governance; a worthy end does not legitimate every means.
projects.capacity: Jurists, administrators, auditors, security specialists and institutional leaders

projects.title: Sustain Livelihood & Life
projects.short: Provide dignified work and the essential goods of a stable common life.
projects.outcome: Reliable and fair provision of livelihoods, care, food, water, housing and infrastructure, with responsible stewardship of resources.

initiatives.name: Essential services
initiatives.example: Healthcare, sanitation, water, food and shelter

initiatives.name: Resilience and stewardship
initiatives.example: Maintenance, environmental care and disaster readiness

projects.method: Determine whether accessible, competent provision is adequate; compare means before constructing new institutions.
projects.capacity: Skilled workers, health practitioners, farmers, engineers, logisticians and employers

warnings: The four projects are a pragmatic editorial synthesis of a large tradition, not a historically fixed canonical classification.
A project or programme does not become obligatory merely by being related to a maqṣad.
An observed shortage does not establish that a particular person must change jobs.
Everyday work and care do not rank lower in spiritual value than high-profile projects.

source_points.title: Ibn Khaldūn: crafts as acquired habits requiring teachers
